facts.statement: Delphyodontos dacriformes is a basal cartilaginous fish found in the Late Mississippian Bear Gulch Limestone of Montana.
facts.quote: Delphyodontos dacriformes is a prehistoric basal cartilaginous fish from the Late Mississippian-aged Bear Gulch Limestone Lagerstätte of Montana.

facts.statement: The adult form of Delphyodontos is unknown because fossils consist only of aborted fetuses or recently born young.
facts.quote: The adult form is unknown, as the only fossil specimens are of aborted fetuses or recently born young.

facts.statement: Evidence of sharp teeth and fecal matter suggests that Delphyodontos practiced intrauterine cannibalism.
facts.quote: Sharp teeth and fecal matter in the fossils suggests that Delphyodontos practiced intrauterine cannibalism.

facts.statement: The genus name Delphyodontos means "womb tooth".
facts.quote: The generic name, Delphyodontos, means "womb tooth".

facts.statement: The originally described fetal specimens measured 35 mm and 29 mm in length.
facts.quote: Two fetal specimens were originally described, measuring 35 mm, holotype) and 29 mm in length.

facts.statement: The body was tadpole-shaped, fully covered in dermal denticles, and featured an enlarged abdomen.
facts.quote: The body, fully covered in dermal denticles, is tadpole-shaped, with an enlarged abdomen.

facts.statement: A 2009 phylogeny found Delphyodontos to be related to the undescribed chondrichthyan ElWeir.
facts.quote: A 2009 phylogeny found Delphyodontos to be related to ElWeir, an undescribed chondrichthyan also known from the Bear Gulch Formation.

facts.statement: Delphyodontos lived during the Serpukhovian, between 326.9 and 323.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Serpukhovian to Serpukhovian (326.9 to 323.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Delphyodontos inhabited a shallow marine bay of tropical waters represented by the Bear Gulch Limestone.
facts.quote: Delphyodontos is known from the Bear Gulch Limestone, a Late Mississippian-aged Lagerstätte from Montana representing a shallow marine bay of tropical waters.

facts.statement: Delphyodontos was a benthic animal with a range extending from the bay mouth to the reef and upper basin.
facts.quote: It was a benthic animal, whose range extended from the bay mouth to the habitat's reef and upper basin.
